messages:
sara.nguyen: Heads-up — acme-inc is hitting intermittent parse failures when using JSON mode streaming on the TS SDK v1.14.2. Error they see: \"SyntaxError: Unexpected token : in JSON at position 0\". They reported this started after we rolled the heartbeat change last week.

ben.johnson: Can you paste the raw stream chunks from the capture? also need SDK logs (DEBUG jsonstream).* 

sara.nguyen: Paste from their tcp capture below (redacted):

```
chunk #1: '{"type":"response","data":"{\"text\":\"hello'
chunk #2: ' world\"}\\n'
chunk #3: ':heartbeat\\n'
chunk #4: '{"type":"response","data":{"text":"ok"}}\\n'
```

sara.nguyen: Notice chunk#2 ends with an escaped newline, then chunk#3 is a lone colon heartbeat. The TS parser seems to treat that colon line as a new JSON line and tries to JSON.parse(":heartbeat") -> fail.

emily.roberts: I can repro locally with both go-sdk and py-sdk when I force chunk boundaries like above. Go's streaming tokenizer currently splits by \n and then calls json.Unmarshal on each line — that fails if the line is just a colon.

allan.kim: This is a protocol mismatch between the new heartbeat marker (we switched to single-colon heartbeats for lower bytes) and the line-based NDJSON parser assumption. We didn't update the SDKs to ignore heartbeat-only lines.

ben.johnson: Quick triage: is the heartbeat always a single colon followed by \n? Or sometimes it's `:\r\n` or `\n:` depending on proxy? Need to make parser resilient to whitespace around it.

sara.nguyen: Customer shows both `:\n` and `:\r\n` depending on platform (CloudFront vs direct). They also reported increased latencies and reconnects right after the error spikes. Might be client-side crash/retry causing the latency complaints.

devex: Proposed short-term workaround for customers: pin server-side to old heartbeat token (we can toggle per-customer) or have them upgrade SDK to a patched pre-release. Longer-term SDK fix: skip lines that match /^\s*:\s*$/ before JSON.parse.

ben.johnson: I put together a minimal patch for TS SDK parser:

```ts
// lib/ndjson-parser.ts
function handleLine(line: string) {
  if (/^\s*:\s*$/.test(line)) return; // heartbeat, ignore
  if (line.trim() === '') return; // stray newline
  try {
    const obj = JSON.parse(line);
    emit(obj);
  } catch (err) {
    logger.debug('ndjson parse fail', { line, err });
    throw err;
  }
}
```

ben.johnson: Patch passes unit tests. But we need to validate against streaming interleaving where a heartbeat lands mid-json (like colon byte arrives before previous newline). The underlying issue is chunk boundary can split JSON tokens. We need a single streaming buffer + newline delimiter assembly.

emily.roberts: In go I changed the reader to use a bufio.Scanner with a custom split that treats a line containing only a colon as a heartbeat and returns zero token. Also added an integration test that sends partial JSON across chunks plus heartbeat lines.

support-bot: Created ticket INFRA-2345: \"streaming: ignore colon heartbeat lines in NDJSON parsers — SDKs\" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1.

allan.kim: Next steps:
- eng-runtime: confirm server heartbeat format and add compatibility note to protocol doc (cc @devex).
- SDKs: backport TS fix to v1.14.x and cut patch release (ben).
- QA: add fuzz tests for chunk boundary interleaving and newline/CRLF combos (emily).
- Support: notify customer and offer temporary server toggle to disable colon heartbeats (sara).

sara.nguyen: I've emailed customer with workaround and asked for their permission to flip the heartbeat toggle. They approved.

devex: I'll update the protocol doc to explicitly say server heartbeats may be a single ':' line and SDKs should ignore lines matching /^\s*:\s*$/ . Also adding example snippet for robust streaming parsing.

ben.johnson: Will open a PR for TS -> release candidate after internal CI passes.

emily.roberts: Verified patched go-sdk on staging against a high-throughput fuzz harness, no parse exceptions after fix.

allan.kim: Marking this resolved from an incident perspective once TS patch released and customer confirmed.

sara.nguyen: Customer confirmed they stopped seeing parse errors and latency spikes after we toggled heartbeat. Closing their support ticket.

devex: Follow-up item: consider switching heartbeat to zero-byte "\n" or dedicated control frames to avoid NDJSON ambiguity. Adding to roadmap. :eyes:

ben.johnson: thx everyone. I'll post links to PR and release in this thread once cut.

support-bot: INFRA-2345 status -> in_progress (assigned: eng-runtime)
